title: Approximate Design-Based Intervals for Downsampled Cross-Sectional Market Aggregates: A Randomized Design for Bandwidth-Constrained Financial Data Pipelines
abstract: arXiv:2610.08801v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Financial institutions routinely downsample cross-sectional options panels to meet bandwidth and cost constraints. The industry default---deterministic Top-$k$ selection by open interest---provides no estimate of the aggregation error it introduces, rendering downstream risk metrics unauditable. We make the identification problem precise. For deterministic rules whose selected set depends only on auxiliary variables and not on the outcome (target-blind rules, of which Top-$k$-by-open-interest is one), the target is not identified from the retained outcomes alone unless bounds or modelling assumptions are imposed; under outcome bounds it is partially identified, with a sharp worst-case interval we characterise in closed form. We propose replacing Top-$k$ with probability sampling whose inclusion probabilities are proportional to open interest, paired with the Hajek ratio estimator and a linearised design-based variance estimator, yielding

translated_title: 降采样横截面市场聚合量的近似基于设计的区间：一种面向带宽受限金融数据管线的随机化设计
translated_abstract: 金融机构为满足带宽和成本限制，通常会对横截面期权面板数据进行降采样。行业默认做法——按未平仓合约量进行确定性 Top-$k$ 选择——无法对其引入的聚合误差给出估计，导致下游风险指标无法审计。我们将这一识别问题精确化。对于所选出集合仅依赖辅助变量而不依赖结果变量的确定性规则（即“目标盲”规则，按未平仓合约量的 Top-$k$ 选择即属此类），若不施加界限或建模假设，目标量无法仅凭保留的结果数据得到识别；在结果变量有界的条件下，目标量仅被部分识别，我们以闭式形式刻画了其尖锐的最坏情况区间。我们提出以包含概率正比于未平仓合约量的概率抽样替代 Top-$k$，并配合 Hajek 比率估计量与线性化的基于设计的方差估计量，从而……
tldr: 该论文指出行业默认的按未平仓合约量Top-k降采样方法无法估计聚合误差且使风险指标不可审计，因而提出改用包含概率正比于未平仓量的概率抽样并结合Hajek估计量，为带宽受限的金融数据管道提供可审计的近似基于设计的区间。
en_tdlr: The paper shows that the industry-standard deterministic Top-k-by-open-interest downsampling leaves the aggregation error unidentified and downstream risk metrics unauditable, and proposes replacing it with probability sampling whose inclusion probabilities are proportional to open interest, paired with the Hajek ratio estimator, to yield approximate design-based intervals for bandwidth-constrained financial data pipelines.
